newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN STRETCH LEAD, DORTMUND TITLE HOPES BURIED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN STRETCH LEAD, DORTMUND TITLE HOPES BURIED.

text.p: Bayern Munich restored their three-point lead at the top of the German Bundesliga on Saturday with their best performance of the season, a 5-0 thrashing of struggling Fortuna Duesseldorf.
But European Cup finalists Borussia Dortmund, missing a clutch of first-team players, saw their hopes of a third successive title finally buried with a 2-0 away defeat by Arminia Bielefeld.
With five matches remaining Bayern now look to have only Bayer Leverkusen, 2-1 home winners over Werder Bremen on Friday, to worry about.
Bayern stamped their authority on the match as early as the sixth minute as Christian Nerlinger drove in from 20 metres to set the Bavarians on the road to their eighth successive home win.
The early goal and Fortuna's obvious weakness appeared to give Bayern the confidence to open up in a way they have not done all season under Italian coach Giovanni Trapattoni.

Juergen Klinsmann delivered a dream pass for midfielder Mario Basler to convert in the 35th minute but both were upstaged three minutes later when Ruggiero Rizzitelli produced a flying scissors-kick to volley home Markus Babbel's cross.

Klinsmann was on hand again to set up Alexander Zickler just before halftime and libero Lothar Matthaeus put the icing on the cake with a solo run seven minutes after the break to score his first goal for 13 months.
It was a different story for Dortmund, missing a further five players from the injury-depleted line-up which beat Manchester United in the European Cup semifinal on Wednesday.
Ottmar Hitzfeld's side were never in the game against Bielefeld, eager to ensure they will not return to the second division after just one season in the first.
Talented midfielder Guiseppe Reina put the home side ahead after just four minutes.

Matthias Breitkreutz made it two in the 40th minute, leaving Dortmund six points off the second place which would give them qualification to next season's Champions' League if they lose their final in Munich next month against Juventus.
VfB Stuttgart had to wait until the 90th minute of their match against Borussia Moenchengladbach to ensure their challenge for second place and outside chance of the title would be maintained.
Substitute Sreto Ristic's header from a Fredi Bobic cross was just reward for the host of chances Stuttgart had produced without being able to get the ball past goalkeeper Uwe Kamps.
Bayern have 62 points from 29 matches, Leverkusen are second on 59, Stuttgart have 55 and Dortmund 53.
Bochum look certain to qualify for the UEFA Cup after coming from behind to beat relegation certainties Freiburg 3-2.
The fight for the final place intensified as both 1860 Munich and Karlsruhe won. Schalke are also in the running despite falling to eighth place after a 1-1 draw against Cologne.
They will hope to make league position irrelevant by beating Inter Milan in the final of this year's competition and qualifying as holders.
